Conditions at observation time: cloudy, no rain, and 65°F. Significant Weather Event reported around 2:00 p.m. on the prior day, 2026-07-29. Temporary flooding observed was similar to Tropical Storm Debby event of 2024 however a much narrower band of St. Lawrence County was impacted. As noted already by NWS Burlington, storms that appeared to have only impacted between and inclusive of Ogdensburg to Hammond, not wider than a 20 mile strip running northeast to southwest. Rain started ~9:00 - 9:30 a.m. and flooding started around 1:30 p.m. Unusually for this time of year, the training rain storm **movement** was northeast to southwest. Rain only occasionally became white-out (or gray-out) conditions. Most of the rain was moderate in intensity, but non-stop for the better part of 4 hours and then continued lighter. Most of the visible ground flooding was gone by this morning, but basements are STILL draining and were quite overwhelmed. Not many fire calls related to flooded basements and there were no power outages. All in all, a nerve-wracking, but easily survivable event.
